categories.main_business_segments: Brown & Brown operates through three main business segments: Retail, Programs, and Wholesale Brokerage. The Retail segment provides a broad range of insurance products and services to commercial, public, professional, and individual customers, as well as non-insurance warranty services through its F&I businesses. The Programs segment acts as a managing general underwriter (MGU), developing and managing specialized insurance programs for niche markets, professionals, and public entities. The Wholesale Brokerage segment markets and sells excess and surplus commercial and personal lines insurance primarily through independent agents and brokers.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary technology platforms, data analytics, and digital tools to deliver insurance and risk management solutions. It utilizes advanced information systems for policy administration, claims processing, and customer engagement, and has adopted artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic process automation (RPA) for operational efficiency. Brown & Brown also employs structured cybersecurity protocols and compliance frameworks to protect sensitive data and ensure regulatory adherence.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Brown & Brown serves a diverse customer base including commercial businesses, public and quasi-public entities, professionals (such as dentists, lawyers, and physicians), individuals, and affinity groups. Its end markets span property and casualty, employee benefits, personal insurance, specialty programs (e.g., flood, earthquake, sports, entertainment), and automotive dealer services. No single customer accounts for a material portion of total revenues, reflecting a broad and diversified client portfolio.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company has a significant presence in the United States, operating in 44 states, with notable concentrations in Florida, Michigan, California, Massachusetts, Georgia, and New York. Internationally, Brown & Brown operates in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Canada, Bermuda, Cayman Islands, Belgium, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Italy, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore, and the United Arab Emirates. In 2024, international operations generated $665 million in revenue.
categories.supply_chain_position: Brown & Brown primarily operates as an intermediary—an insurance agent and broker—positioned downstream in the insurance value chain. It does not generally assume underwriting risk, except for limited participation in captive insurance facilities and a write-your-own flood insurance carrier, where risk is largely ceded to reinsurers or government programs.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic priorities include organic growth, targeted acquisitions, digital transformation, and expanding specialized insurance programs. Brown & Brown invests in technology, cybersecurity, and data analytics to enhance customer experience and operational efficiency. It is focused on innovation in product offerings, leveraging AI and automation, and maintaining a decentralized, high-performance culture to drive growth and adaptability.
categories.revenue_model: Brown & Brown generates revenue primarily through commissions paid by insurance carriers, which are typically a percentage of the premiums placed. It also earns fees for certain services, including third-party claims administration, policy issuance, and consulting. Additional revenue streams include profit-sharing contingent commissions based on underwriting results, and, to a lesser extent, investment income and limited underwriting profits from captive insurance participation.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company competes with large global and national insurance brokers such as Marsh McLennan, Aon, Willis Towers Watson, and Arthur J. Gallagher, as well as regional brokers and direct-to-consumer insurance providers. Brown & Brown is positioned as a leading, growth-oriented intermediary with a strong track record of acquisitions and organic expansion, but faces competition from both traditional brokers and technology-driven entrants.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Brown & Brown reported total revenues of $4.8 billion and net income attributable to the company of $993 million. The company has demonstrated consistent growth, with a 12.1% increase in commissions and fees and a 10.4% organic revenue growth rate in 2024. Over the past three decades, it has achieved a compound annual revenue growth rate of 13.5%, driven by both acquisitions and organic initiatives.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Brown & Brown differentiates itself through a decentralized, customer-first culture, deep industry expertise, and a broad portfolio of specialized insurance solutions. Its value proposition centers on responsive service, tailored risk management, innovative program development, and strong carrier relationships. The company emphasizes agility, local market knowledge, and a meritocratic, ownership-driven culture to deliver superior results for clients and partners.
